scope: Optimizers and weight-space procedures that use curvature or norm geometry: Fisher-based preconditioning, Kronecker-factored and spectral-norm updates and the routines that compute them, and Fisher-weighted consolidation or merging of trained weights. Not general training recipes, learning-rate schedules or architectures.

concepts.title: Kronecker-factored preconditioning
concepts.definition: Preconditioning a layer's matrix-shaped gradient with the Kronecker product of two small per-dimension matrices, so that a full-matrix preconditioner is approximated with memory and compute that scale with each dimension rather than with their product.

evidence.phrase: a separate preconditioner matrix for each of the gradient's dimensions
the Kronecker product of the two root matrices
a Kronecker product of two smaller matrices
the optimal Kronecker approximation of Adagrad
the left and right Shampoo preconditioners
Kronecker products of much smaller matrices

near_pairs.name: Kronecker-factored approximate curvature
near_pairs.why: K-FAC is the Fisher-based instance of the same Kronecker factorization; the reader decides whether the general idea (Shampoo, SOAP, K-FAC) deserves its own note or folds into K-FAC.

concepts.title: Newton-Schulz orthogonalization
concepts.definition: An iterative odd-polynomial matrix routine that pushes every singular value of a matrix toward one, approximating its semi-orthogonal factor UV^T without an SVD, and so computes spectral-norm steepest-descent updates such as Muon's.

concepts.title: Elastic weight consolidation
concepts.definition: A continual-learning regularizer that adds a quadratic penalty anchoring each weight to its value after earlier tasks, with a stiffness set by the diagonal Fisher information, so weights important to old tasks change slowly while the rest stay free to learn.

relations.quote: the Fisher information matrix is computed at each task switch to form a new EWC penalty

concepts.title: Fisher merging
concepts.definition: Merging models that share an initialization by averaging their parameters with per-parameter weights given by each model's diagonal Fisher information, which maximizes the joint likelihood of their Gaussian approximate posteriors.

relations.quote: Fisher merging uses the diagonal of each model's Fisher information as the precision matrix
